sentences.text: Acrodus was an extinct genus of hybodont sharks named for its high, tooth-like features. It was a durophagous predator, meaning it ate hard-shelled prey, using blunt, broad teeth to crush and grind food.
Some Middle Triassic species are suggested to have reached lengths between 1.8 and 2.5 meters.
The genus was originally described by Agassiz in Alberti in 1834.
However, the name was formally assigned by Louis Agassiz in 1938.
Scientists have recorded 170 fossil occurrences of this genus to date.
Acrodus species inhabited both marine and freshwater environments, though all Middle and Late Jurassic species are known only from freshwater.
Taxonomically, Acrodus belongs to the kingdom Animalia, phylum Chordata, class Chondrichthyes, order Hybodontiformes, and family Acrodontidae.
This shark lived from the Asselian to the Thanetian stages, spanning from 298.9 to 56 million years ago.
